notes: Read all 121 numbered source lines before editing. Native port follows the established dashboard idiom (ChargingOptimizerWidget / BatteryHealthAnalyticsWidget): every not-yet-ported web dependency (WidgetShell, WidgetFlowDiagram, DataFreshness, EmptyState, numberFormat, react-i18next, lucide-react) is reproduced inline native-safe with RN primitives + shared native components and documented here.

L1 `import { useMemo }` -> native `import {useEffect, useMemo, useState}` (useEffect/useState added for the inline 30s freshness tick). L2 react-i18next useTranslation('dashboard') -> module-level English-default `t(key, fallback, vars?)` with {{var}} interpolation, keeping every widget.* / freshness.* key verbatim.

L3 lucide-react Activity/BatteryCharging/Zap/Plug -> no native icon font: each reduced to a representative glyph with the exact web hex colour preserved — Activity '\u223F' (text-neon-cyan -> native `accent` token #35d5ff, ActivityGlyph in the shell header), BatteryCharging '\u26A1' (emerald-400 #34d399, battery node), Zap '\u26A1' (purple-400 #a78bfa, motor node), Plug '\u2393' (amber-400 #fbbf24, charger node). NodeIcon renders the glyph in the supplied colour; the EmptyState Activity icon is dropped (native EmptyState has no icon slot).

L4 feedback EmptyState imported from ../../../../components/feedback/EmptyState; web's single `message` becomes native `title`, native `message=''` (web `icon`/`className=py-4` have no native EmptyState slot and are dropped — energy signal kept in the header glyph). L5 useVehicles + useVehicleState imported unchanged from ../../../api/hooks/useVehicles (same /vehicles and /vehicles/{id}/state paths, same snake_case shape, same 5s refetch).

L6 @/lib/numberFormat fmtNumber -> inlined verbatim with safeNumber guard, default precision 2, en-US grouping (the unconfigured web default since useSettings is not wired in native). L7 './WidgetShell' -> inline `WidgetShell` (subset). L8 './shared' WidgetFlowDiagram + FlowNode/FlowArrow -> inline native `WidgetFlowDiagram` + local FlowNode/FlowArrow types. L9 './types' WidgetProps -> local `WidgetProps`/`WidgetSize` (only vehicleId read, matching the web destructure).

L7/L10-inline WidgetShell honours exactly the props this widget passes (title, icon, loading, updatedAt, isFetching, isStale, isError, onRefresh): loading -> skeleton (testID energy-flow-loading); error -> centred errorBox + retry Pressable mirroring web <QueryError> (testID energy-flow-error, unused here since the widget passes no `error`); titled -> header (ActivityGlyph + uppercase 11px muted title + WidgetFreshness) over body (testID energy-flow-widget); title-less branch kept for shell fidelity (overlay freshness top-right) though this widget always passes a title.

DataFreshness 4-state chip reproduced inline as `WidgetFreshness`: same isError>fetching>stale>fresh precedence, FRESHNESS_DOT tiers (emerald-400/sky-400/amber-400/red-400), the just-now/Nm/Nh/Nd/Nw relative ladder, updating…/error labels, a 30s re-render tick (cleared on unmount so --detectOpenHandles stays clean), and onRefresh wired to a Pressable (role=button; testID energy-flow-freshness).

L8 WidgetFlowDiagram is an SVG (positioned node circles + variable-stroke animated <line>s) which RN can't render without react-native-svg (not a dependency) -> reproduced as a native flex layout: the SVG POSITION_COORDS map (top/left/right/center/bottom) becomes a top row / left|center|right main row / bottom row of FlowNodeChips; each <line> becomes a FlowArrowRow whose proportional fill-bar width tracks |value|/maxArrowValue and whose bar height reuses the ported `strokeForValue` (MIN_STROKE 1..MAX_STROKE 4); `resolveArrowColor` reproduces web `arrowColor` (override wins, else >0 emerald-400 / <0 red-400 / 0 muted, mapped class->hex); the web animated dash (active) is shown as full-opacity vs 0.3-dimmed bar. nodeMap, the compact arrow sort-by-|value|+slice(0,3), maxArrowValue=Math.max(...|value|,1), the nodes.length===0 EmptyState fallback (testID energy-flow-diagram-empty), and the compact label slice(0,3).toUpperCase() are all ported verbatim. compact defaults false (the widget never passes it).

FlowNodeChip mirrors the web node: a circle with node.icon + the value. Web renders <AnimatedNumber value={node.value} decimals={1} /> (NOT formattedValue), so the chip shows fmtNumber(node.value, 1); the richer node.formattedValue is preserved and surfaced via accessibilityLabel. testID energy-flow-node-{id}.

L11 default export EnergyFlowWidget({vehicleId}: WidgetProps) + displayName. L12 useTranslation('dashboard') -> inline t (the unused-here `t` instance is folded into the module-level helper). L13 const {data: vehicles} = useVehicles() preserved. L14 id = vehicleId ?? vehicles?.[0]?.id ?? 0 preserved verbatim.

L15 useVehicleState(id, {refetchInterval: 5_000}) destructured as data:stateData/isLoading/isFetching/isStale/isError/dataUpdatedAt/refetch — names preserved verbatim. L16 state = stateData?.state: the native hook types state as VehicleState|string|null, so it is narrowed (`rawState != null && typeof rawState === 'object'`) to the object form; runtime on this path only ever yields a VehicleState object or undefined, so the field reads + the `{state ? ...}` render guard behave exactly as the web (documented deviation: a non-object string state, which the API never returns here, falls to the EmptyState instead of an undefined-field diagram).

L18-24 power = state?.power ?? 0; isConsuming = power > 0; isRegen = power < 0; absPower = Math.abs(power); isCharging = state?.is_charging ?? false; chargerPower = state?.charger_power ?? 0; batteryLevel = state?.battery_level ?? 0 — all preserved verbatim.

L26-62 nodes useMemo<FlowNode[]>: battery node (id 'battery', label t('widget.battery','Battery'), value batteryLevel, formattedValue `${batteryLevel}%`, NodeIcon ⚡ emerald-400, position 'left'); motor node (id 'motor', label isConsuming->t('widget.consuming','Consuming') / isRegen->t('widget.regenerating','Regenerating') / else t('widget.standby','Standby'), value absPower, formattedValue absPower>0 ? `${fmtNumber(absPower,1)} kW` : '—' (native '\u2014'), NodeIcon ⚡ purple-400, position 'right'); when isCharging push charger node (id 'charger', label t('widget.charger','Charger'), value chargerPower, formattedValue `${fmtNumber(chargerPower,1)} kW`, NodeIcon ⎓ amber-400, position 'top'). Dep array [batteryLevel, absPower, isConsuming, isRegen, isCharging, chargerPower] — web also listed the stable `t`; native `t` is module-level so react-hooks/exhaustive-deps omits it, identical output.

L64-93 arrows useMemo<FlowArrow[]>: battery->motor (value isConsuming?absPower:0, active isConsuming, color 'text-cyan-400'); motor->battery (value isRegen?absPower:0, active isRegen, color 'text-emerald-400'); when isCharging push charger->battery (value chargerPower, active true, color 'text-amber-400'). Dep array [absPower, isConsuming, isRegen, isCharging, chargerPower] preserved verbatim.

L95-120 return <WidgetShell title=t('widget.energyFlow','Energy Flow') icon={<ActivityGlyph/>} loading={isLoading} updatedAt={dataUpdatedAt} isFetching isStale isError onRefresh={()=>refetch()}>: when `state` -> <WidgetFlowDiagram nodes arrows emptyMessage=t('widget.noEnergyData','No energy data available')/>; else -> EmptyState(noEnergyData) wrapped in a testID energy-flow-empty View (web Activity icon + py-4 dropped). L121 closing brace -> default export + displayName.

Companion __tests__/EnergyFlowWidgetParity.test.tsx mocks useVehicles/useVehicleState and renders: loading skeleton; consuming (Battery/Consuming, Battery → Motor active, 12.5 kW); regenerating (Regenerating, Motor → Battery); standby (power 0); charging (Charger node + Charger → Battery amber, 7.0); empty (no live state -> energy-flow-empty + 'No energy data available'); vehicleId fallback to first vehicle id; explicit vehicleId prop forwarded to useVehicleState with {refetchInterval:5000}; freshness chip present. Every test unmounts so the 30s freshness interval leaves no open handle.

Gates run from apps/native: npm run typecheck (tsc --noEmit), npm run lint -- --quiet (eslint .), npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles (jest). No DOM, react-router, framer-motion, lucide-react, Recharts, Leaflet, or old web UI components are imported into the native output.
